title: Grothendieck transfer through creation and exactness of orbit sums
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal V$, a Grothendieck abelian category $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] relative to $\mathcal V$, and a locally $\mathcal V$-small abelian category $\mathcal B$ [def-sp-abelian]. Let $U:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be additive, faithful, exact and conservative, creating all $\mathcal V$-small colimits, and let $A:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive left adjoint. For any generator $G$ of $\mathcal A$, $A(G)$ is a generator of $\mathcal B$: here generator means that every proper subobject $N\subsetneq X$ is missed by some map from the generator to $X$. Filtered colimits in $\mathcal B$ are exact, so $\mathcal B$ is Grothendieck abelian. In addition assume given additive exact autoequivalences $P_n:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$, $n\in\mathbf Z$, and a natural isomorphism $UA\cong\bigoplus_nP_n$, where the sum is taken pointwise. Then $A$ is exact. Explicitly, for every small family of short exact sequences $0\to X_i\to Y_i\to Z_i\to0$ in $\mathcal A$, the sequence of their coproducts is short exact. For each family $(X_i)$ the canonical maps from finite subsums identify $\bigoplus_iX_i$ with $\operatorname{colim}_{J\subseteq I,\,J\text{ finite}}\bigoplus_{i\in J}X_i$. These identifications are natural in maps of families and identify kernels and cokernels of finite subsum sequences and their filtered colimits with the corresponding direct-sum sequences. Consequently $UA$, and hence $A$, preserves short exact sequences.

Finite subsets use finite biproducts, filtered finite subsets use [lem-sfb-grothendieck-filtered-finite-limits], and full coproducts use AB4 from step 7. Cokernels are preserved since colim is a left adjoint. All are Mathlib canonical comparisons, so the universal-property identifications of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] are retained.

proof.text: Set Q := Discrete.functor P. For each integer n, extract preservation of finite limits and colimits from the exactFunctor hypothesis [def-galois-exact-functor]. Evaluation of Q.flip is definitionally P_n; preservesFiniteLimits_of_evaluation and its colimit dual prove Q.flip exact. The colimit functor on Discrete Z is exact by AB4 (shrink the available colimit universes to zero). Thus Q.flip followed by colim is exact. The natural isomorphism colimitIsoFlipCompColim Q identifies this functor with the pointwise coproduct of the P_n. Transport exactness through this isomorphism and e to L followed by U. Since U reflects finite limits and finite colimits by exactness and conservativity, preservesFiniteLimits_of_reflects_of_preserves and its colimit dual give exactness of L. Finally ShortExact.map_of_exact gives both short exact sequence conclusions in the convention of [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].
